# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline

Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
  context is already large.

## This machine runs concurrent sessions

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.
- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

## Creative triad

For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
timeline files or approve their own implementation.

Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.

Durable contracts live in:

- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`

# ch13 survey standby stall — read-only source audit

Recorded 2026-09-06T14:41Z. Read-only mechanical auditor. **Not** an acceptance, not a
repair authorization, not live browser proof. Companion: `standby-source-audit.json`.

All 98 manifest files rehashed before (14:34:29Z) and after (14:40:25Z) this audit: all
98 match `implementation-source-manifest.json` both times, before == after. Nothing in
`main/`, `docs/`, the contract, the capture tree or any defect record was written.

## The question

The movie completes every drawn corner (42 samples, 35.31 route units, tested prefix 41)
and then freezes on the rail plan `walk -> (-42, 51.05, 9)`, reason *"standing clear of the
span he is testing"*, while W-7744 holds on `body-clearance`.

## The four captured values that constrain any answer

| value | captured |
|---|---|
| `finalState.autopilot.routeAction` | `direct` |
| `finalState.autopilot.stillTime` | `0` |
| `finalState.autopilot.teleportNudgesTotal` | `0` |
| player pose | exactly unchanged for the whole stall window |

`direct` is not `unreachable` and not `idle`; `stillTime 0` with `nudges 0` means the stuck
watchdog never armed, which in `primitives.ts:2400` can only happen if **no movement control
was pressed**. Any explanation in which the body is pushing against a wall is excluded by
these two numbers alone.

## Candidate cause (independently derived from frozen source)

The standby target is arithmetic, not authored geometry:

```ts
// commonGroundDirector.ts:1950
const CG_STANDBY_CLEAR_OF_E = { x: E.x, y: E.y, z: E.z - 3 };   // (-42, 51.05, 9)
```

It is not in `CG_POSES` and not on any of the three routes. `CommonGroundWorld.tsx`
plants **no** ground — `createFooting` reads live terrain — so every authored pose sits at
y = 51.05 because that site was *qualified* against real terrain. This target never was.

With `VOXEL_SCALE = 2`, `worldToGrid` puts z = 9 in the cell centred at **z = 10**; the body
stands in the cell centred at **z = 12** — one cell away. Then, in
`agentSurfaceNavigation.ts`:

1. `:420` — a requested goal cell that is **not dry** is silently replaced by the nearest
   dry cell in ordered-offset order, radius 8 cells = 16 world units. **The body's own cell
   is inside that set.**
2. `:651` — candidates are tried **nearest-first, not cheapest-first**, and the start cell
   is trivially reachable.
3. `:742` — `if (chosen.path.length === 1 && mode === 'walk') { mode = 'direct'; reason = 'already-at-resolved-goal' }`.

Downstream, in `primitives.ts`:

4. `:1546` — `route.mode === 'direct'` ⇒ **`routeAction = 'direct'`** ✅ matches capture.
5. `:1222` — the sub-cell exact-goal rescue **refuses** (`goal-outside-terminal-cell`):
   z = 9 vs terminal centre z = 12 is 3 units, far outside the half-cell bound.
6. `:1607` — the single waypoint is the body's **own cell centre**, so `steerFreeToward`'s
   0.2 dead zone clears forward/backward/left/right. **No input is ever issued.**
7. `:2400` — `pushing === false` ⇒ **`stillTime = 0`**, and the unstick escalation, which
   requires `pushing`, never runs ⇒ **`nudges = 0`**. ✅ both match capture.
8. `walkToward` still measures 3.16 units > the 0.6 stop radius, so **arrival is never
   declared** and the rail republishes the identical plan every frame.

The other half of the deadlock is authored and correct: `commonGroundActor.ts:249` blocks
his *next* step when the horizontal gap to her would fall under 1 unit (measured separation
now 1.0026), and he is deliberately never allowed to displace her. Neither body can move.

## Ruled out

- **`world-navigation-unavailable`** and **`different-face-direct-fallback`** also report
  `direct`, but both set the waypoint to the *goal*, so input would be pressed — excluded by
  `stillTime 0` / `nudges 0` (and faces match here anyway).
- **`unreachable` route** — would report `routeAction: 'unreachable'`.
- **Physical obstruction while pushing** — that is precisely what the watchdog counts; both
  counters are zero.
- **`screeningSettling()`** — sets `idle`.
- **Arrive radius 0.6 being too tight** — the gap is 3.16, not marginal. No threshold
  weakening is implied, proposed or acceptable.
- **"Press F Reopen"** — explicitly not inferred. Reopening the tail removes neither the
  non-traversable standby column nor the 1-unit clearance geometry; the same plan would be
  republished the moment she is again on his span.

## What is still unmeasured

*Why* the cell at (-42, ·, 10) is not dry — water, a ceiling inside `clearanceCells`, no
support column, hazard, or the `edgeMarginCells` test — is **not established**. Root's
water/cliff pixels in raw0054 are *consistent* with it but prove no footing and no cause,
and this audit does not lean on them. The planner's actual `reason` string is inferred from
`mode === 'direct'` plus exclusion of the other two direct-producing branches; the capture
records the action, not the reason. **No live terrain sample, route replay or browser
measurement was taken.** A CPU-only reproduction was scoped and deliberately **not run**:
the only run-local seed (3215739679, world `-1,-1`) belongs to the partial-continue fixture,
is not proven to be survey-movie-1's world, and `planetSize` is not recorded in the capture —
the number would have looked like proof of the wrong world.

## Smallest live discriminator

One read-only frame at the existing stall pose: call
`planAgentSurfaceRoute(terrain, planetSize, playerPos, (-42,51.05,9))` and log
`{ mode, reason, waypoints.length, resolvedGoal, requestedGoalWasWet, visitedCells }`, plus
the classification (support height, dry, wet, waterDepthCells, bodyBlocked) of the cells
centred (-42,10), (-44,10), (-40,10), (-42,8), (-42,12). `reason:'already-at-resolved-goal'`
with `waypoints.length === 1` confirms the cause outright; `requestedGoalWasWet` then
separates water from blocked/unsupported. No mutation, no progress setter, no threshold
change. A CPU-only variant first needs the capture to record that world's seed and planetSize.

## Repair scope — recommendation only, nothing authorized

- **A — author the standby pose** (`commonGroundDirector.ts:1950`): stop deriving it from
  `E.z - 3`; qualify it like every other pose, on plateau the chapter already stands on
  (e.g. the z = 14..22 side of the long route, comfortably >1 unit off his span). Smallest
  blast radius, no shared-code change.
- **B — surface the degenerate route** (`agentSurfaceNavigation.ts:742` + `walkToward`): a
  resolved goal that *is* the start cell, while the requested goal is still beyond the
  caller's stop radius, is a refusal, not a route. Reporting it as one turns this whole class
  of silent freeze into a named failure. Shared navigation code — belongs to that module's
  owner and needs its own regression evidence. It does not by itself make the point reachable.
- **C — qualify rail targets at publish time**: run any rail walk target through the footing
  predicate the chapter already trusts before publishing it. Closes the general gap that poses
  and routes are terrain-qualified while *derived* targets are not.

None of these may be implemented as a weakened threshold, relaxed footing, endpoint credit or
teleport rescue.

**The generic same-system handoff works. It commits to Origin. The chapter world binding reclaims the departure world one render later.**

Root cause is one absent table entry, `main/src/story/tidegardenRoute.ts:128-131` (`e7237efc…`):

```ts
const CROSSING_DESTINATION_WORLD_ID = {
  'ch8-crossing': TIDEGARDEN_WORLD_ID,
  'ch10-ask': STORY_PRIMARY_WORLD_ID   // 'ch13-return' missing
};
```

**Executed reproduction** (CPU-only, shipped module bundled out-of-tree, no game change): with a *committed* crossing (`currentWorld=activePlanet=-1,-1`), `resolveStoryRuntimeWorldId` answers `-1,-1:p1` for ch13-return, while the identical ch10-ask control stays on Origin. That is executed, not traced.

**Both epoch increments are now proved, not guessed**, from telemetry you already own:
- ep3→4 = `commitSystemPlanetHandoff` — proved by `renderOrigin` becoming `[0,0,0]` (Origin) with `atmosphere` + `target:null`; this also closes the discriminator's open question: the transient `activePlanetId === '-1,-1'` **did** exist in the unsampled gap.
- ep4→5 = `setActiveSystemPlanet('-1,-1:p1')` — proved because `renderOrigin` **stayed** `[0,0,0]`, which excludes both the handoff and the interstellar reset.
- Call site is `ShipController.tsx:472-473`, not `EfficientScene.tsx:648` — the latter would have forced `locationMode:'surface'`, and it stayed `atmosphere`.

**Smallest seam:** add `'ch13-return': STORY_PRIMARY_WORLD_ID`. One symbol. The guard already requires the handoff to have committed, so it grants no milestone, teleport, targetReady bypass, tolerance or speed. I explicitly reject the alternative of adding it to `originOwnedBeat`, which would boot Continue onto Origin without flying. No geometry/agency/copy/AV change.

Every authored pose and route vertex in ch13 sits on **even** x/z, i.e. exact voxel-cell centres (`VOXEL_SCALE 2`, `worldToGrid = round(c/2)`). `E.z-3 = 9` is the chapter's **only off-lattice target**, and 9 is the *boundary* of the z=10 cell — a full 3.0 units from the body's terminal cell centre. So the handoff is impossible by construction, independent of whether that cell is dry. The unmeasured question (why `(-42,·,10)` was rejected) is now separated from the structural one; note `W = (-34,51.05,10)` proves the z=10 row isn't globally unusable.

**Yes, a standby can be derived from existing footprint:** `CG_ROUTE_LONG` already contains `(-42,51.05,18/20/22)` — walked in survey-movie-1, on-lattice, off the common route and off the E→H leg by 2–6 units (vs. the 1-unit clearance rule). `(-42,51.05,20)` is preferred. Reusing a signed route vertex means no new geometry, no copy/agency/AV change, and no shared navigation edit.
